pages.transcription:
AEROGRAMMA
VIA PANAIR

Saturday, 25.I.41.

First part
Dear Hanna & Manfred,
I find it somewhat difficult to give
you to-day already a definite opinion
about Eva's stay at Salmon's. I saw her
yesterday and to-day - shall meet Mrs. S.
on Monday in town - and can only say that
perhaps the surrounding atmosphere - in
cluding Mr. and Mrs. S - is somewhat dull
in comparison with all she saw and
heard and learned in your house and also
in Bath. They seem to be very kind with
Eva and she said she liked them both
- on the other hand ~~the~~ I suppose she
would have spoken differently of people
like for instance Raumanns. She just
finds them nice and likes it there
without being enthusiastic. But I
feel certain that this „liking“ is
real on her part, and so, even if we
should decide that it is better to
move her to another place you can
be quite reassured that no harm has
been done and that she has been quite
satisfied in friendly surroundings, even
though from an intellectual point of
view they were not ideal. - As to the
school Eva told me that the teacher
pages.notes: Handschriftlicher Brief auf einem Aerogramm-Formular. Die Tinte ist gut lesbar.

pages.transcription:
had suggested that she should go already
to a high school instead of the one she is
in now - so that may give an easy
excuse for a change, if necessary.
In any case please don't worry
about this any more. We are near and
will look after her and only feel sorry
that owing to our own uncertainty we
cannot take her to live with us.
So these are our general first
impressions, and now you can turn
over to the other part in which I
just tell you about Eva. I thought
you might want first to know
our impression before you read what
we did together and how she lives.
Lotte

AEROGRAMMA
VIA PANAIR

Read the other letter Newyork, 25.I.41
Dear Mummy. first
I was with Uncle Stefan and
Auntie Lotte today. It was very
nice. I hope you are well.
Love
and
kisses
Eva.

Dear Hanna & Manfred, I made Eva
begin the letter as a visual proof to you
that we have been together. I saw her yester-
day for an hour at New Rochelle - there was a
snowstorm and I had to leave earlier and
got out later than intended. Mrs. Salmon was
not at home, but I cannot blame her for it
for she rang me up inviting me to dinner
or to postpone my visit as she would be out.
But I wanted to see Eva, so I went out
and arranged to meet Mrs. S. for lunch on
Monday (I shall report on that as well, of
course). As to the surroundings: New Rochelle
is a suburb, very nicely situated in midst
of trees and woods, and the house looks out
on a little lake where there was skating.
Eva has got a pair of skates and begun to
learn already. As the skating started only
this week she cannot yet be an expert, but
she seemed to like it. - I stayed with her in
pages.notes: Zweites Blatt des Briefes. Enthält einen kurzen Abschnitt von Eva und den Beginn des Haupttextes von Lotte.

pages.transcription:
a lovely sitting-room, a huge window over-
looking the little lake, the room with modern
and tasteful furniture, a baby grand piano,
a huge Alsatian dog and the little boy
Peter - a nice-looking boy of 3 - crawling
about, too shy to speak. Eva herself was
a little bit shy too, in the beginning, and
I can in a way understand it; for me too,
it was a strange experience, coming to see
her as a visitor, where we had been living
a common life, so to speak. As I said, I
stayed about an hour, talking to the maid
which is nice, listening to a prelude of
Chopin for Eva did not want to play
me the Beethoven. She told me that the
teacher was much stricter than Miss
Luton, always picking out the difficult
parts for her to study specially - like
daddy. She likes the teacher but I
do not quite understand why this teacher
makes her play the Moonshine Sonata
and Chopin preludes if on the other
hand she takes it seriously. Eva said the
teacher had told her that the Moonshine
sonata was easy and that she could play
it. Well, I did not hear it, only the Chopin
prelude which she played quite well,
although rather too painstakingly. I also

saw her room which is very nice, has a writing
table and a terrace and all one wants. The
house itself seems not bigger than auntie
Ine's in Coverdale Road, but is in a good
neighbourhood and tastefully furnished as
far as I saw it. As to the little boy Eva
says that she does not play too much
with him because he bores her, which
seems quite normal in view of the difference
of age. She has a number of school friends
which she apparently sees quite a lot, but
she could not give any answer to my
motherly question (which I myself had always
hated to be asked) what their parents were
and which their father's profession. - In case
Eva has not given you a description of her
day, here it is: getting-up at 8 breakfast
at 8 1/2 (chocolate and roll) school at 9, lunch
in Salmon's house, school again and at
4 again at home. Then she reads,
afterwards practises, at 7 Mr. S. comes
home, Mrs S. is mostly at home, Eva says,
then they have dinner, afterwards Eva
does her homework and is in bed about
9. - Eva looks well and has grown some-
what, was wearing that check dress on
Friday and Saturday the red velvet dress
which now fits her perfectly. Saturday
Eva spent the day with us as fortunately
the piano lesson did not take place as
usually on Saturday mornings. She came

to the hotel, later we had lunch together
(potato salad!), then I took her to a studio
tour through the Radio. Then we went
back to the hotel and stayed there
until it was time for her to go
back. There is a kind of taxi service
out to New Rochelle, which takes about
one hour and brings one from house to
house, running every hour and accomo-
dating 6 passengers. That is very convenient
as Eva does not need any company for the
way because she is fetched at home and
brought directly to her destination,
which before usually was Zweig's and
now is our hotel.
As to ourselves we feel already
rested and Stefan is longing to begin
work again. We hardly have seen any-
body except Huebsch and my brother-
in-law, and & except a few people whom
we met in the street we have remained
so far anonymous and enjoy it. I hope
to hear soon from you c/o Viking Press
and expect also one or two letters for-
warded again from Brazil.
Kindest regards to all,
love to you,
Lotte.
